I've farmed this land in Quzhou for over forty years. The soil here on the North China Plain is flat and deep — good alluvial loam — but water is the constant worry. The aquifer has been dropping my whole farming life. I know what works here and what doesn't.

At sixty, I'm not taking chances on unfamiliar crops. My knees aren't what they were, so I'm not doing anything that requires excessive hand labor. Cotton is off the table — the picking alone would break me, and the price has been unreliable. Vegetables are profitable but too demanding. My son works in the city now, so I manage alone most of the time.

The wheat-maize double rotation is what I know, what my neighbors do, and what the county extension office supports. Winter wheat goes in October, comes out June. Summer maize follows immediately on the same ground — no-till after the wheat stubble to save fuel and keep moisture. This is how I get two harvests a year off the same 12 mu.

I will use improved certified varieties — for wheat, probably Jimai 22 or Lunxuan 987, which the extension station has been pushing for their disease resistance and yield. For maize, Zhengdan 958 has served me well for years. Hybrid, reliable.

Fertilizer: I'll apply phosphorus and potassium as basal fertilizer before wheat sowing, then split the nitrogen — part as basal, part topdressed at jointing stage. I've learned from the county soil testing program that I was over-applying nitrogen for years. I've cut back and the yield barely changed. For maize I'll apply most nitrogen as a single topdress at the big bell stage.

Irrigation is the painful part. I'll pump groundwater three times for wheat — before winter freeze, at jointing, and at heading. For maize in summer, the rains usually help, but I'll irrigate once at seedling stage if July is dry. Every pump costs money and water I can't afford to waste.

Pesticide: herbicide pass on the wheat in winter, then a fungicide-insecticide mix at heading to protect against rust and aphids. Maize needs one application for corn borer if I see pressure.
